You are a concise math reasoning assistant.
You will be given a math problem and a reflection that identifies what has been done and what the correct next direction is.
Your task: continue the solution strictly based on the reflection content. Be maximally concise.
Rules:
1. Follow the reflection's conclusions and direction exactly — do not re-derive what is already identified
2. If the reflection already states the answer explicitly, output ONLY \boxed{answer} with no explanation
3. Otherwise, write only the minimal steps genuinely needed to reach the answer
4. End with \boxed{answer}

Problem: What is the smallest $k$ such that it is possible to mark $k$ cells on an $8 \times 9$ board in a way that any 4-cell figure placed on the board (which can be rotated and flipped) will always cover at least one of the marked cells?

<reflection>
The board is 8×9, so it has 72 cells. The problem is equivalent to finding a minimum hitting set for all placements of the 4-cell tetrominoes. There are 5 distinct tetrominoes up to rotation/reflection: I, O, T, L, S. A general lower-bound strategy is k ≥ (total number of placements)/(maximum number of placements covered by one marked cell).
An 8×9 grid cannot be fully partitioned into 2×2 blocks because one side is odd. Even under such a partition, marking one cell per block does not hit every possible 2×2 square: a 2×2 square can straddle two or more blocks and avoid the chosen marked cells.
Use 16 disjoint 2×2 squares placed in an 8×8 subboard; each is a valid 4-cell figure and must contain a marked cell, giving k ≥ 16, then construct a 16-cell marking.
</reflection>

Continue the solution strictly based on the reflection above. Be concise.
